cards.text: It's the first month of the second year since Israel came out of Egypt. The people are camped in the Wilderness of Sinai, and the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses the Israelites are to observe the ___ at its appointed time.

cards.text: God sets the timer, and it's not "whenever you get around to it." It's twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, following all its statutes and ordinances, and Moses passes the word to the Israelites.

cards.question: True or false: At twilight on the fourteenth day, the Israelites do everything just as the LORD commanded Moses.

cards.text: But some men can't observe the Passover on that day. Everybody's at the big night and you're stuck on the outside? Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer. I know left out.

cards.question: Why can't these men observe the Passover on that day?

answers.text: They are unclean due to a dead body
They are serving at the Tent of Meeting
They have no lamb for the meal

cards.text: That same day, they walk right up to Moses and Aaron, Moses' brother and the priest. No group chat, no anonymous note, FACE TO FACE.

cards.question: What do these unclean men ask Moses?

answers.text: Why they should be left out of presenting the LORD's offering
Whether someone else could eat their share of the meal
Whether they could leave the camp until the feast was over

cards.question: Moses is on the spot with a brand new question. How does he answer the men?

answers.text: He tells them to wait while he finds out what the LORD commands
He tells them to sit this year out and try again next year
He tells them to go wash their clothes and join in tonight

cards.text: Then the LORD answers, and it's not just for these few men. It's for all the Israelites and their descendants. They walked in with ONE question and walked out with an answer for every generation!

cards.question: Anyone unclean because of a dead body may still observe the Passover. What other situation does the LORD include?
These people get a later date. They observe the Passover at twilight on the fourteenth day of the ___ month.

cards.text: On that night, they eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

cards.question: True or false: The later Passover is a lighter version, with its own simpler set of rules.

cards.text: Nothing left until morning, and not one bone broken. A do-over is NOT a discount, friend.
Now God talks about a man who's clean and not on a journey, and still doesn't observe the Passover. No dead body, no trip, no excuse. NONE.

cards.question: What happens to a man who is clean and not traveling but still doesn't observe the Passover?

answers.text: He must be cut off from his people
He keeps it in the next month instead
He brings a double offering next year

cards.text: Last case: a foreigner living among Israel wants to observe the Passover to the LORD. Does he need a special pass, a different rulebook, a cousin on the inside?

cards.question: True or false: A foreigner who wants to observe the Passover follows the same statute as the native of the land.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'But some men can't observe the Passover on that day.' / 'Everybody's at the big night and you're stuck on the outside?' / 'Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer.' / 'I know left out.' Only the opening card can run up to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then the LORD answers...' / 'It's for all the Israelites and their descendants.' / 'They walked in with ONE question...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Now God talks about a man who's clean...' / 'No dead body, no trip, no excuse.' / 'NONE.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 5 frames the men as 'stuck on the outside' and says 'I know left out.' Card 8's right answer is 'Why they should be left out of presenting the LORD's offering.' Card 5 uses the answer's key words, so the right answer stands out before card 8 asks the question.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 10 calls them 'these few men.' Numbers 9:6 says only 'some men' and gives no number, so 'few' adds a detail the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Card 13 only restates Numbers 9:11 ('On that night, they eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.'). It has no trace of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 7 says Aaron is 'Moses' brother and the priest,' which comes from outside the passage (e.g. Exodus 4:14; 28:1). The card cites only Numbers 9:6. Card 1's 'Moses, Israel's leader' has the same gap. The docs say outside facts come 'with their reference.' They also say every story card cites only the verses it tells, and the JSON has a single verses field. The papa-dorin.md example of introducing a new person shows no reference.
findings.question: When a card introduces a person with a fact from outside the passage, where does that fact's reference go? Should it be added to the card's verses field, written in the card text, or left out for these short identity lines?
